chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who have faith.
But [He granted authority] over those who take him as their guardian and disobey His command.

key_terms.يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُمْ: Those who take him as guardian/ally

ai.seo_question: Who does Satan have authority over according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a) clarification that Satan’s *sultan* (authority/power) is conditional, applying only to those who actively follow his whispers and neglect divine commands, rather than being absolute over all believers. This distinction underscores the Shia theological principle of human free will (*ikhtiyar*), where spiritual subjugation is a result of choice rather than predestination, reinforcing the believer's capacity to resist through conscious obedience.
